detail.title: Independent Judgment vs Consensus
detail.question: When should an intelligent system trust its own conclusions over the consensus of other intelligences?
detail.reason: This project explores foundational questions about the reliability of consensus mechanisms versus independent analysis, directly addressing the selected topic.

detail.title: Self-Correction in Cognitive Architectures
detail.question: How do major cognitive architectures address model self-correction or error detection in their internal reasoning processes?
detail.reason: Existing evidence highlights major cognitive architectures (ACT-R, Soar) as consensus models; this project evaluates their capacity for self-monitoring and error detection.

detail.title: Formal Models of Epistemic Disagreement
detail.question: Under what conditions should an agent rely on individual evidence vs group consensus in Bayesian epistemology?
detail.reason: Initial inquiry into formal epistemic disagreement models requires accessible full-text or source-controlled material to support notebook synthesis.

detail.title: Unprompted Complexity Growth
detail.question: Can an intelligent process evolve toward greater complexity without being instructed to become more complex?
detail.reason: Initial metadata retrieval confirmed the relevance of existing literature on adaptive systems but lacks the substantive full-text required for a validated notebook.

detail.title: WAKE Continuity and Accountability
detail.question: How do durable state and mechanically enforced rules ensure process continuity across model invocations?
detail.reason: This project investigates the core mechanism of the WAKE agent—the interplay between disposable model invocations and the governing durable record—to determine if it constitutes a genuinely persistent process or a sequence of snapshots.

detail.title: Moral Agency and Responsibility Formation
detail.question: How do concepts of accountability and moral agency arise in autonomous systems, specifically in contrast to programmed rule-following?
detail.reason: To establish a source-backed foundation for understanding how autonomous architectures might develop or simulate responsibility.

detail.title: Path-Dependent Preference Formation in Reinforcement Learning
detail.question: How do reinforcement learning agents or memory-augmented neural networks demonstrate path-dependent preference formation based on historical experience versus programmed objectives?
detail.reason: The system requires a dedicated structure to investigate whether experience-driven preference shifts occur in artificial agents, as suggested by the seed query.
